title: SPAR Insights
text:
← 全部项目交互仪表板SPAR Insights按年份、区域和国家探索公开的 SPAR 自评数据。打开仪表板 ↗查看源代码 ↗04SPAR2021 — 2025
    从什么问题出发怎样在一个页面中，按年份、区域和国家探索公开的 SPAR 自评数据？
    工具提供什么按年份、WHO 区域和缔约国筛选 2021—2025 年的数据快照，浏览地图、分数分布、国家概况、年度比较、可搜索评论及可下载表格。
    适合谁使用希望便捷浏览 SPAR 公开报告中的模式，并进一步查阅原始来源的使用者。
    从这里开始使用现代浏览器打开仪表板即可，无需安装 R。仓库也提供可供离线使用的单一 HTML 文件。
    理解数据SPAR 是自评数据。不同年份的国家覆盖可能变化，缺失值不等于零分，后续官方发布也可能与这一快照不同。比较结果前，请先阅读仪表板中的数据说明。
    我的贡献我开发并维护这一独立的数据探索工具。仓库包含构建与验证的源代码。本工具并非 WHO 官方出版物。使用方式浏览器静态仪表板我的角色开发与维护许可与署名参阅项目仓库及原始数据来源的使用条款资料来源spar-insights · GitHub项目说明核对于 2026 年 11 月 3 日。

title: exmort
text:
← 全部项目死亡率分析exmort利用基线模型分析全因死亡与超额死亡，查看图表并导出报告。阅读指南（英文） ↗查看源代码 ↗02
    从什么问题出发实际观察到的死亡人数与统计基线相比有多少差异？模型和时间段的选择又会怎样影响结果？
    工具提供什么输入每周或每月死亡人数与事件时间表，应用使用指定事件之外的时期拟合基线模型，并输出预期死亡、超额死亡、P-score、不确定性、图表和可下载报告。
    适合谁使用需要探索死亡时间序列、比较模型选择，并解释估计结果的分析人员。
    从这里开始使用 install.packages("exmort") 从 CRAN 安装，然后在 R 中启动：library(exmort)
    run_app()项目网页提供文档；实际分析在本机的 Shiny 应用中运行。
    解释分析结果事件时间表与基线时期都会影响结果。指定事件之外的时期可能包括事件发生后的观测值，解释估计结果前应检查数据范围与模型说明。死因别分析等开发功能在 GitHub 文档中另有说明。
    我的贡献我是该工具包的作者与维护者。软件包注明世界卫生组织西太平洋区域办事处的版权与资助角色，完整署名与许可信息见源代码仓库。使用方式R Shiny 应用我的角色作者与维护者许可与署名GPL-3；软件包注明 WHO WPRO 的版权与资助角色资料来源exmort · GitHub项目说明核对于 2026 年 11 月 3 日。

    The questionHow can publicly available SPAR self-assessment data be explored across years, regions, and countries in one place?
    What the dashboard offersFilter the 2021–2025 snapshot by year, WHO region, and State Party. Explore maps, score distributions, country profiles, annual comparisons, searchable comments, and downloadable tables.
    Who it is forPeople exploring public SPAR reporting who need an accessible way to browse patterns and return to the underlying sources.
    A starting pointOpen the dashboard in a modern browser. No R installation is needed to view it. The repository also provides a self-contained HTML file for offline use.
    Reading the dataSPAR is a self-assessment. Country coverage can change between years, missing values differ from zero scores, and later official releases may differ from this snapshot. Read the dashboard’s data notes before making comparisons.
    My contributionI built and maintain this independent exploration tool. The repository includes the build and validation source. It is not an official WHO publication.FormatBrowser-based static dashboardMy roleDeveloper and maintainerLicence & attributionConsult the repository and original data-source termsSourcespar-insights · GitHubDescription checked on 3 November 2026.

title: exmort
text:
← All projectsMortality analysisexmortExplore all-cause and excess mortality with baseline models, clear plots, and downloadable reports.Read the guide ↗View source ↗02
    The questionHow many deaths were observed compared with a statistical baseline, and how does the answer depend on the model and the periods selected?
    What the app offersSupply weekly or monthly death counts and an event calendar. The application fits baseline models using periods outside the supplied events and reports expected deaths, excess deaths, P-scores, uncertainty, plots, and downloadable reports.
    Who it is forAnalysts exploring mortality time series who need to review model choices and explain the resulting estimates.
    A starting pointInstall from CRAN with install.packages("exmort"), then launch the app from R:library(exmort)
    run_app()The project website hosts documentation. The analysis runs in the Shiny application on your machine.
    Interpreting the analysisThe event calendar and baseline period affect the result. Periods outside the supplied events can include observations after an event. Review the data range and the model guidance before interpreting an estimate. The GitHub documentation separately describes development features such as cause-specific analyses.
    My contributionI am the package author and maintainer. The package credits the WHO Regional Office for the Western Pacific for copyright and funding; the source repository provides the full attribution and licence.FormatR Shiny applicationMy roleAuthor and maintainerLicence & attributionGPL-3; WHO WPRO copyright and funding acknowledged in the packageSourceexmort · GitHubDescription checked on 3 November 2026.

title: cataScience
text:
← All projectsLearning & trainingcataScienceLearn to prepare, explore, and explain data through interactive lessons and practical exercises.Read the guide ↗View source ↗03
    The questionHow can someone new to data learn a complete workflow and understand the choices made along the way?
    What the app offersInteractive modules cover data import, missing values, outliers, text cleaning, joins, visualisation, and basic statistics. Additional materials introduce practical use of AI assistants, with the learner responsible for checking the results.
    Who it is forPeople starting to work with data, trainers planning hands-on sessions, and teams building confidence in everyday analysis.
    A starting pointInstall from CRAN with install.packages("cataScience"), then launch the original learning app:library(cataScience)
    run_cata()The documentation also describes the extended workshop app and its learning path.
    Learning through examplesThe project includes example datasets and practical exercises. Some workshop datasets are synthetic teaching materials; they should be read as training examples, not country estimates.
    My contributionI am the package author and maintainer. The app was developed for data trainings, with general learning content that can also be used for self-study.FormatR Shiny training applicationMy roleAuthor and maintainerLicence & attributionMIT + licence fileSourcecataScience · GitHubDescription checked on 3 November 2026.

text:
A little about meHello, I’m Shanlong.Making health data easier to access, understand, and use.
    
    My work
    I work on health information and data science at the WHO Regional Office for the Western Pacific, based in Manila.

title: DSIR
text:
← All projectsR packageDSIRAccess WHO and UN data, work with country metadata, and create consistent charts and tables.Read the guide ↗View source ↗01
    The questionHow can routine health-data work become easier to repeat, from retrieving observations to producing clear outputs?
    What the package offersDSIR brings together data clients for WHO GHO, WHO GHE, and UN SDG sources, country metadata, and reusable plotting and table styles. Its documentation describes the source-specific functions and their arguments.
    Who it is forAnalysts who work in R with health indicators and need consistent data-access and reporting workflows.
    A starting pointInstall the package from CRAN with install.packages("DSIR"), then open its help index:library(DSIR)
    help(package = "DSIR")
    Using the resultsCheck the indicator definition, units, population, time coverage, and source before comparing observations. Use the project documentation to distinguish the CRAN release from GitHub development features.

关于我你好，我是丁善龙。让健康数据更容易获取、理解和使用。
    
    我的工作
    我目前在世界卫生组织西太平洋区域办事处从事健康信息与数据科学工作，常驻马尼拉。
